notes: ⭐ 19/09/2026: THE APIARY ROSTER TEXT WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED (Dean re-confirmed: "orange means GROW everywhere", "make it a Grow"). This entry's `actionText` used to print "Sow 1 card from your hand onto one of your buildings", which described a SOW - place a card, activate nothing - and that has not been the ruling since M7 (12/09/2026, shipped 14/09/2026 evening): an Apiary Worker's plain action is a GROW, exactly the ordinary Grow task (pay 1 card matching the target building's activation cost, gain its ability; a full building is never a legal target). `actionText` now says so. ⚠️ THE DISPATCH WAS NEVER WRONG - only the printed sentence was. `meepleActionOf` (packages/engine/src/workers.ts) already maps this door's `sow` action to `grow` whenever `rules.turn.meepleSpendTiming` is `'afterAction'`, which is the shipped value, and `performDoorAction`'s existing `grow` case already pushes the ordinary Grow task chain (`growOptions`/`doGrow`) - proven by packages/engine/src/delivery-meeple.test.ts's M7/M8 cases, which passed before this note was written and are unchanged by it. ⛔ `id` AND `action` STAY `sow` ON PURPOSE, EVEN THOUGH THE PRINTED SENTENCE NO LONGER SAYS SOW: `action` is typed `WorkerAction` (packages/data/src/types.ts), which is deliberately five-wide and does not include `grow` - `DoorAction` is the wider type for what a door COMPUTES to, never what its roster entry PRINTS - and widening it would touch `doorArt`'s asset lookup (no `grow.webp` exists), `ACTION_LABEL` in packages/ui/src/view/table.ts, and the v31 control's tested inertness (packages/engine/src/testkit.ts `cardVisitGame()`, whose apiary meeple must keep buying its literal Sow at `meepleSpendTiming: 'start'` - packages/engine/src/delivery-meeple.test.ts's 'leaves the v31 apiary meeple buying a Sow'). None of that is this fix's job. What WAS this fix's job: packages/ui/src/components/Meeple.tsx's `WORKER_ACTION_LABEL` and packages/ui/src/components/Supply.tsx's `workerAction()` apiary special case existed only because this sentence lied; both now compute the label through `meepleActionOf` instead of overriding it, so a further rules change here cannot go stale under them again.

⚠️ 13/09/2026: THE COMMONS IS DELETED (Dean), and with it the central boards and the Apiary board's `actionUnderCommons` GROW payload. Notes below that describe the commons as the shipped game are history; the shipped game is rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower', where a visit buys a board's printed power (rules.economy.noticeBoardPower) rather than the door action in this file.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: THERE ARE NOW THREE READERS, NOT TWO, AND THE THIRD IS THE SHIPPED GAME. Under rules.turn.visitCurrency 'commons' the five Notice Boards sit OWNERLESS IN THE CENTRE of the table and any player may play a card onto one to buy its action, so a door belongs to the table rather than to a seat. `linkedSuit` still says which suit a board wears; it no longer says who owns it. The other two readers - a seat's own Notice Board under 'card', a meeple of that colour under 'meeple' - survive as the controls. THE FIVE DOORS (Dean, 02/09/2026, v31). This file is the one place that says what each suit's action IS. Everything else in the game reads it from here, and there are now exactly two readers: a suit's NOTICE BOARD grants the action to whoever places a card on it, and a MEEPLE of that colour performs the same action, free, when its owner spends it at the start of a turn. Same five entries, same five actions, two ways in.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31. What left the file in one edit: serviceThreshold, ownerActivationCost and visitWage, plus every enhancement the roster carried. If you are reading a note or a report written before 02/09/2026 that mentions a Service starter, a hire fee, a Working Week, a wage ladder or an enhanced door, it is describing a game that no longer exists.

THERE IS NO SERVICE CARD, AND NOW THERE IS NO SERVICE. The fourth starter went on 20/08/2026 when the door merged into the Notice Board; the last of its vocabulary goes here. serviceThreshold is deleted because the door's threshold is the Notice Board's, printed on the card and overridden by rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold, and one number in two files is how the 5-versus-2 drift happened the first time. ownerActivationCost is deleted because there is nothing to pay it with and, more to the point, because the owner is no longer a special case: in v31 the owner places a card on their own board exactly as a rival does, threshold and all. visitWage is deleted because there are no coins to mint - the payment to the owner was already 0 and already the FREIGHT, which is the one part of the old economy that survives intact.

THE DOORS ARE PLAIN, AND THAT IS THE CHANGE. Every entry below performs its suit's action exactly as the core action performs it, with one marked exception. The enhancements the doors used to carry (a relaxed harvest, a hand card into the barn before a delivery, a deck-sown card, a build at a discount of 2 with the crop requirements waived) are all gone. The reason is that the bonus slot itself became the enhancement: a door now buys a WHOLE CORE ACTION for one card, which is a far bigger prize than any of those riders ever was, and stacking a rider on top of it was pricing a sweetener into a deal that no longer needed one. It also collapses five paragraphs of teach into one sentence - 'place a card, take that suit's action' - which is what a five-minute teach is for.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: THE EXCEPTION IS GONE FROM THE SHIPPED DATA. `draw` is 2/2 and the Orchard door is plain, which is Dean's choice of 2 over 3 (C3). Read the paragraph below as the argument the v31 control still runs on, and note what it does NOT say: it assumes the bonus slot's alternative is a FREE Draw 1, and the commons has no free option at all - the slot holds one thing and it costs a card. ⚠️ THE HALF OF THE ARGUMENT THAT SURVIVES IS THE FEE. A commons play costs one card, so a Draw 2 board returns 2 for 1 and nets +1 where every other board hands back a whole action for the same card. That is the thinnest return in the set and it is why overlays/commons-draw-three.overlay.json exists. overlays/orchard-door-draw-two-v1.overlay.json is now a NO-OP against the shipped data and is kept only because four reports name it. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE ORCHARD DOOR, AT DRAW 3, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The self-cancellation law is the reason: a visitor pays 1 card to use a door, so a door whose action PRODUCES cards has to over-deliver or buying it is net zero. In v31 the yardstick got higher, because the bonus slot's other option is a free Draw 1 (rules.turn.bonusDraw). A plain Draw 2 door would cost 1 card and return 2, netting +1 - exactly what the free option gives for nothing - so it would be STRICTLY WORSE than the alternative and the Orchard board would take no traffic at all. Draw 3 nets +2: pay your worst card, draw three, and the door is card-positive against the free option by one card. That is the whole margin the door has. If anybody ever tidies this to Draw 2 for consistency with the other four, the Orchard door dies overnight, and it will die silently - nothing will error, the traffic will simply go somewhere else. overlays/orchard-door-draw-two-v1.overlay.json is the paired control that measures exactly this.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: NO SUBJECT UNDER THE COMMONS - there are no meeples in the shipped game (C6). The five entries are still listed regardless of the seat count, and now for a stronger reason than the one below: under the commons all five BOARDS are on the table whatever suits are in play, so every action is buyable in every game. A MEEPLE IS THE SAME ACTION WITHOUT THE CARD. It is drawn face up onto an island delivery space at setup, claimed with that delivery, spent one at a time at the start of a later turn, and then leaves the game for good. A meeple of a suit that is NOT at the table still works, which is why this file lists all five entries regardless of the seat count and why island.json deals its bag from all five colours: the five actions exist independently of who farms what. The colour-to-action map is therefore here and nowhere else, and island.json says so explicitly rather than copying it.

RULING (carried over, unchanged since v13): suit powers apply to actions performed through a door or by a meeple. It is your action, whoever's premises it is taken on and whatever wooden thing paid for it.

`name` IS FLAVOUR ONLY. These five names were printed on the Service cards that no longer exist, and nothing in v31 prints them - the door is printed on the Notice Board and the meeple is a colour. They are kept because the UI and the reports read better with a name than with an action id, and because renaming them is a design decision this file is not entitled to make on its own. Treat them as labels awaiting a ruling, not as card titles.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: READ ONLY BY THE MEEPLE CONTROLS, and note that its 2/2 and the shipped `draw`'s 2/2 are now the same number arrived at by two different arguments - the meeple arm's because a visit costs nothing, the commons's because Dean chose 2 over 3. Do not collapse the two payloads into one on the strength of that coincidence: the v31 control still needs `draw` at 3/3. drawUnderMeepleCurrency IS THE ORCHARD DOOR'S SECOND PRINTED PAYLOAD, READ ONLY UNDER rules.turn.visitCurrency 'meeple' (Dean, 04/09/2026, rule R2). `draw` at 3/3 keeps driving the shipped 'card' game and MUST NOT be edited to move the arm, or the control moves with it. Under the arm the door is a plain Draw 2, and the whole of the reason for the exception has gone with the fee: Draw 3 existed because a visit cost a CARD, so a door that produced cards had to over-deliver against a free Draw 1 or buying it was net zero. A meeple visit costs no card and the free standalone Draw 1 does not exist, so the self-cancellation law has nothing left to bite on and every one of the five doors is the plain base action again. Sweep it back to 3/2 as a control if the Orchard slot takes an implausible share of visits.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: NOT UNDER THE COMMONS. Nobody owns a board, all five are in the centre, and the table's menu of buyable actions is therefore the same five in every game whatever suits were chosen. `linkedSuit` reads as the board's COLOUR under the commons and as ownership under the two controls. linkedSuit is ownership in the door sense: the seat playing that suit owns that Notice Board and nobody else does, so the table's menu of buyable actions is decided by which suits were chosen. It is NOT ownership in the meeple sense - anybody may hold and spend a meeple of any colour.
unresolved: THE ORCHARD BOARD AT DRAW 2 IS THE ONE CONTESTED DOOR NUMBER (Dean chose 2 over 3, 09/09/2026). Every other board hands back a whole action for the card played; Draw 2 hands back two cards for one, netting +1. The prediction is that the Orchard board goes dead and overlays/commons-draw-three.overlay.json is the falsifier. If it collapses at 2 and thrives at 3, the exception the card visit needed has come back under a different argument, and it will have come back in a game with no free draw for it to beat.

THE ORCHARD EXCEPTION IS THE ONE ASYMMETRY IN AN OTHERWISE FLAT SET, and it is defended by arithmetic rather than by measurement. The arithmetic is sound (Draw 2 ties the free option, Draw 3 beats it by one card) but nobody has yet run the arm that shows the Orchard board taking MORE traffic than the other four in proportion, which is what would say the margin is right rather than merely non-zero. If Orchard runs away with the door mix, the dial is this number and not the Orchard suit's cards.
The Apiary door's hand-sow, above. Ruled, not settled.

Whether a door should ever refuse a visitor who cannot use it. A Wheat door with no full building to harvest, a Vegetable door with an empty barn, a Dairy door with nothing affordable: the visitor pays a card and gets nothing. In v30 that was rare, because the doors were enhanced and the enhancements mostly applied; with plain actions it is a live case at every board. Nothing in the data expresses a legality check, and the engine will have to rule it one way or the other.

A10 The Cross-Pollinator printed 'HIRE a Hired Worker, paying GBP 1 less', which has been text for a rule that does not exist since 2026-08-10 and is now text for a currency that does not exist either. It is a card, so it belongs to the sheet and to cards.json, but it is recorded here because this file is where the referent died.
